absent: Internal algorithms for current deadline accounting, load averaging, leftmost selection, high resolution tick start, push and pull queuing, preemption comparison, and bandwidth add or subtract primitives.
Full layouts of runqueue, deadline runqueue, task, deadline entity, root domain, bandwidth object, affinity context, and scheduler domain structures beyond fields named in these fragments.
Locking contracts for runqueue clock, sequence file output, debugfs creation or removal, inode handling, cpuset access, and housekeeping mask publication.
Global realtime period or runtime sources, ratio conversion, per-runqueue bandwidth ratio initialization, visited-domain tracking, and common bandwidth manager behavior.
Timer lifecycle for inactive and non-contending states, cpuset deadline counting rules, and wakeup or reschedule propagation outside these callbacks.
Scheduler feature enumeration values, tunable scaling factor derivation, normalized sysctl set, cache topology refresh effects, preemption mode identifiers, and debug file permission semantics.

findings.text: Periodic tick for deadline tasks refreshes current execution accounting and load average, then re-arms a high resolution tick only when that facility is enabled for the runqueue, the tick arrived in queued context, the task retains positive remaining runtime, and the task remains the earliest deadline entity.
Fork handling for the deadline class performs no work because deadline tasks are prevented from forking by an earlier common fork path.
Retry bound for deadline push or pull search is three attempts.
A per-CPU scratch CPU mask exists for deadline bandwidth and placement calculations, allowing callers to obtain a temporary mask without dynamic allocation on the current CPU.
Runqueue push helper repeatedly attempts to migrate a deadline task until one attempt reports no movement, so a single invocation drains all immediately pushable work.

Wakeup path for deadline tasks triggers a push only when the woken task is not on this CPU, the current task is not already marked for rescheduling, the woken task is migratable, the current donor is deadline, and either current is not migratable or the woken entity does not preempt the donor entity.

Affinity change for a deadline task checks whether migration crosses root domains and if so removes the task bandwidth contribution from the source domain bandwidth object while holding that object lock, before delegating to common affinity handling.
Bandwidth move predicate is true only for deadline tasks whose supplied new mask has no overlap with the span of the task current root domain.

Runqueue online transition restores overload marking if the deadline runqueue was overloaded and publishes either the earliest deadline or a cleared entry in the root domain capacity structure depending on whether deadline tasks remain; offline transition clears overload marking and clears the capacity entry.

Effective CPUs for deadline bandwidth first consults housekeeping domain configuration: when domain housekeeping is active and the task allowed mask is disjoint from it, the result is all active CPUs outside housekeeping; otherwise the result comes from the locked cpuset allowed query.
Housekeeping query reports whether a given housekeeping type flag is set in global housekeeping state using a single atomic read.

Root domain join adds the task deadline bandwidth to the bandwidth object of the domain containing the first active CPU in the task effective mask, skipping non-deadline and special entities, and expects at least one usable CPU to exist.

Root domain join holds the task priority inheritance lock with interrupts saved across the whole selection and accounting sequence, and additionally holds the destination domain bandwidth lock only around the bandwidth increment.
Server bandwidth helper adds fair server and optionally extension server utilization to a root domain only when the server entity is a deadline server, is currently attached, and the CPU is active.

Root domain clear resets total bandwidth to zero and restores each member runqueue extra bandwidth to its maximum, then explicitly re-adds deadline server contributions for every CPU in the domain span.
Root domain clear serializes with a scoped guard on the domain bandwidth lock with interrupt state saved; the per-CPU variant simply forwards to the domain variant for the caller CPU domain.

Leaving deadline class starts non-contending handling for queued tasks with configured runtime, decrements cpuset deadline count, removes running and runqueue bandwidth when the task is not queued, clears the non-contending marker to avoid later use after migration, and pulls work when this was the last queued deadline task.

Joining deadline class cancels any inactive timer, increments cpuset deadline count, adds runqueue bandwidth and returns when not queued, otherwise either updates load when the task is the donor or issues push and preemption or reschedule actions depending on migratability, overload, and donor class.
Deadline priority query refreshes current execution state when the queried task is the current donor and then returns the entity absolute deadline.

Deadline change handling ignores non-queued tasks and unchanged deadlines, pulls from overloaded peers when the deadline moved later, and requests rescheduling when an earlier deadline now exists either on the runqueue earliest entry or relative to current.
Throttle query for a deadline task reports the entity throttled flag without consulting the supplied CPU identifier.

Global deadline validation computes desired bandwidth from global realtime period and runtime, advances a global cookie used to visit each root domain once, and reports busy if any visited domain already holds more total bandwidth than the new limit allows for its CPU count.

Global validation iterates online CPUs under scheduled read-side critical sections, skips already visited domains via the cookie, and holds each domain bandwidth lock with interrupts saved only while comparing limits.

Global deadline apply computes a new bandwidth ratio unless global runtime is unlimited, reinitializes every possible CPU deadline bandwidth ratio, then stores the new limit into each distinct root domain exactly once identified by an incremented cookie.

Deadline parameter store copies runtime, deadline, and period with period defaulting to deadline when unspecified, masks flags to the deadline subset, and derives bandwidth and density ratios from period and deadline respectively.

Deadline parameter fetch always returns priority, period, and masked flags; in dynamic mode it also returns live remaining runtime and a wall-clock adjusted absolute deadline after refreshing runqueue clock and current state, otherwise it returns configured runtime and deadline.
Dynamic parameter fetch holds the runqueue lock with interrupts disabled while updating the runqueue clock and current deadline state.
Bandwidth request enumeration distinguishes deactivation, allocation, and release operations with successive small integer values starting at zero.
Bandwidth allocation and release wrappers forward the CPU and bandwidth amount to a common manager with the corresponding request operation, with allocation propagating the manager result.
Nanosecond formatting helpers split a 64-bit value into whole milliseconds and remainder milliseconds, preserving sign so negative inputs yield a negated quotient and a positive remainder.

Scheduler feature names table is generated from a shared feature list by stringizing each feature identifier, and the parallel static key table is generated from the same list by selecting an initially true or false key initializer.
Feature display writes each feature name preceded by a negation marker when its bit is clear in the global feature mask, separated by spaces and terminated by a newline.

Feature toggle parses an optional negation prefix, matches the remainder against known feature names, then either clears or sets the corresponding global mask bit and disables or enables the matching static key; unknown names propagate a lookup failure.

Feature control write truncates user input to a small bounded buffer, strips surrounding whitespace, and serializes the toggle under CPU hotplug read lock with the file inode lock held; failure to toggle propagates without advancing the file offset.
Debug interfaces for features, scaling, cache control, and preemption mode each expose open, read, write, seek, and release operations backed by single-open sequential file helpers.

Scaling control parses an unsigned integer from user input, rejects values at or beyond the defined end marker, stores the validated mode, and only advances the file offset when a follow-up scaling refresh succeeds.
Scaling refresh recomputes normalized base slice state by dividing the configured base slice by a factor obtained from update policy and always reports success.
Cache control write parses a boolean from user input, stores it in the user cache preference, triggers a topology-wide cache active refresh, and then advances the file offset.
Cache active refresh serializes topology changes by acquiring CPU hotplug read lock outermost and scheduler domains mutex innermost around the internal refresh.
Cache active refresh lock order is hotplug read protection first, then domains mutex, with release in reverse order.
Preemption mode control accepts a short bounded string, resolves it to a mode identifier, rejects unknown names, and only advances the file offset after successfully applying the new mode.
Preemption mode display enumerates supported modes within a compile-time constrained range, marking the currently active mode with surrounding parentheses.

Verbose domain debug toggle holds hotplug read lock and domains mutex while updating the global verbose flag, creating domain debug entries when enabling and removing the top domains directory when disabling.

Domain debug rebuild does nothing before debug infrastructure exists or while verbose mode is off, lazily allocates and initializes the pending CPU set, creates the top domains directory once, then rebuilds one per-CPU directory and numbered per-domain subdirectories while consuming the pending set.
Per-domain debug registration publishes timing, cost, and policy fields plus read-only name, flags, group flags, level, and conditionally an asymmetric packing preferred CPU entry.
Root domain join treats absence of any active CPU in the effective mask as a fatal invariant violation rather than returning an error.
Affinity change warns once when invoked on a non-deadline task but continues execution, and global validation can transiently fail callers when bandwidth is being moved between domains.
Debug writes fail cleanly on user copy faults, unparsable booleans or integers, out-of-range scaling values, and unknown feature or preemption mode names.
